$comment: Supabase advisor findings that are correct for this project.
Keys are the `cache_key` the Management API returns for each finding.
Checked by `npm run check:advisors`. Every entry needs a reason saying why
the finding is right, not why it is inconvenient. A key that no longer
matches any finding fails the check too, so exceptions cannot rot.

accepted.rls_enabled_no_policy_public_number_sequ: Deny-all by design. Gapless per-org numbering is allocated only by app.next_number(), a SECURITY DEFINER function; `authenticated` holds no privilege on the table at all. A policy here would be the bug.
accepted.authenticated_security_definer_function_: Definer on purpose: it links a pending invitation to the caller's user_id and bumps their claim epoch, both of which require writing rows the caller has no policy for. Guarded by auth.uid() and the caller's verified email.

Definer on purpose: `organizations` has no INSERT policy, because an org must never exist without an owner membership. This function creates both in one transaction, which is exactly why direct inserts are withheld.

Definer on purpose: a portal contact has no INSERT or UPDATE policy on `jobs`. It checks app.portal_contact_for() and writes the status transition as actor_kind 'client', which is the attribution staff cannot forge.
Definer on purpose: it writes `approvals`, where `authenticated` holds SELECT only so the record is append-only. Refuses a viewer contact, an already-decided quote and an expired one before writing.
Definer on purpose, same as approve_quote: append-only `approvals` and the client-attributed job transition.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_jobs: Two audiences, one table: jobs_staff_select (app.staff_orgs()) and jobs_portal_select (app.portal_clients(), drafts excluded). Supabase has a single `authenticated` role, so two permissive policies is how staff and contacts coexist. Merging them into one OR'd policy would hide which audience each half serves.

jobs_staff_update (dispatch roles) and jobs_tech_update (a tech, restricted to jobs where lead_tech_id = auth.uid()). Deliberately separate: the tech branch carries an extra row condition that must not apply to dispatchers.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_clie: clients_staff_select and clients_portal_select. Same two-audience reason as jobs.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_site: sites_staff_select and sites_portal_select. Same two-audience reason as jobs.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_quot: quotes_staff_select (dispatch roles only -- techs read nothing priced) and quotes_portal_select (drafts excluded).
quote_line_items_staff_select and quote_line_items_portal_select, which additionally checks the parent quote is not a draft.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_appr: approvals_staff_select and approvals_portal_select. A contact reads their own decisions; staff read their org's.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_orga: organizations_staff_select and organizations_portal_select. A contact needs the org's name and branding for the portal shell.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_clie: client_contacts_staff_select, client_contacts_self_select (user_id = auth.uid(), so a contact sees only their own row and cannot enumerate colleagues) and client_contacts_auth_admin_read (supabase_auth_admin, for the access-token hook).
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_cata: catalog_items_staff_select plus the dispatch-role write policy, whose FOR ALL form also covers SELECT. Left as is: the two are not redundant in the way the note tables' were, because the read policy is the narrower of the pair.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_job_: job_evidence_staff_select (app.staff_orgs() -- every staff role, techs included, because recording and reading field evidence is their work) and job_evidence_portal_select (client_visible only, own client, non-draft job). Same two-audience reason as jobs: one `authenticated` role has to serve both.

job_evidence_author_update (a tech, restricted to rows where captured_by = auth.uid(), so they can fix their own caption or retract their own photo) and job_evidence_dispatch_update (dispatch roles, any row in the org, because deciding what the client sees is their call). Deliberately separate: the author branch carries an extra row condition that must not apply to dispatchers. Same shape as jobs UPDATE.
accepted.authenticated_security_definer_function_: Definer on purpose: it writes `approvals` (where authenticated holds SELECT only, so the record is append-only) and performs the work_complete -> client_accepted transition, whose only registered actor_kind is 'client'. Refuses a viewer contact and an already-signed-off job before writing.

Definer on purpose, same as accept_completion. Records the rejection and deliberately moves nothing: there is no client edge out of work_complete for a rejection, so a person decides what happens next.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_invo: invoices_staff_select (dispatch roles only -- techs read nothing priced) and invoices_portal_select (own client, drafts excluded). The usual two-audience shape forced by a single `authenticated` role.
invoice_line_items_staff_all (dispatch roles; its FOR ALL form also covers SELECT) and invoice_line_items_portal_select, which additionally checks the parent invoice is not a draft.
accepted.multiple_permissive_policies_public_prof: profiles_self_select (user_id = auth.uid(), always available so a user can read their own profile even with no memberships) and profiles_org_mates_select (the profile of someone who shares an org with the caller, scoped through org_members on both sides, which is what lets the team settings page show names instead of a column of blanks). Deliberately separate: the self branch must not depend on membership, and the org-mates branch must not widen to strangers.

conditional.auth_leaked_password_protection: PRO-PLAN GATED, not a design decision. PATCH /config/auth {password_hibp_enabled: true} returns HTTP 402 "available on Pro Plans and up", and the setting is not expressible in config.toml with this CLI version (four candidate keys probed, none produced a diff; the CLI silently ignores unknown keys, so no error there means nothing). It appears whenever the project has users, so it will be present in production. Mitigations: the app offers magic links only and has no password field anywhere, minimum_password_length is 12, and password_requirements demands mixed case, digits and symbols. REVISIT ON UPGRADE: enable it and delete this entry. CONDITIONAL: this finding only appears once the project has users, so it is dormant whenever the database is empty (as it is after a test run). Recorded here rather than deleted, because deleting it would mean the next person to create a user meets an unexplained CI failure.
